speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that history. To better understand the cause of your fatigue, night sweats, and weight loss, can you tell me if you have noticed any changes in your appetite or bowel habits, and do you have a history of smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That weight loss is significant. Have you noticed any lumps in your neck, armpits, or groin, and have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or chest pain? Also, have you noticed any blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fixed, painless supraclavicular lymph node combined with your "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss) is highly concerning for lymphoma. I need to see the node and check your blood work. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: CBC with Differential and LDH.

Abdominal Examination: Inspection shows slight abdominal distension; Auscultation reveals normal bowel sounds; Percussion indicates dullness over the left lower quadrant; Palpation detects splenomegaly without rebound tenderness. Blood Work: Complete Blood Count shows Elevated WBC, Slightly Decreased Hemoglobin, and Normal Platelets; Lactate Dehydrogenase is Elevated. Imaging: CT Scan of Thorax and Abdomen shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy: Cervical Lymph Node findings include lymphocytes with a high proliferative index staining positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unexpected result given the classic presentation of painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and elevated LDH with CD20 positivity, which strongly points to a B-cell lymphoma. However, since you have been diagnosed with Tuberculosis, do you have any known contact with someone who has an active infection, or have you traveled to an endemic area?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sensation of tightness in your clothes suggests ascites or significant organomegaly, which can accompany advanced lymphoma. Given the biopsy showed CD20 positivity, this confirms a B-cell origin, likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. Have you noticed any specific skin rashes or itching in recent days?

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). Your history of heavy smoking, combined with the fixed supraclavicular lymph node, splenomegaly, "B symptoms," elevated LDH, and the biopsy showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index, confirms this aggressive B-cell malignancy.
